# testdata

Fixtures that tests read, borrowed from Go's `testdata/` convention. V has
no convention of its own here.

Rules:

- Tests only **read** from here. Nothing in `v test` writes to it.
- Every file records where each value came from: the source (book and
  table, paper, database and version, or tool and version), and the date
  it was generated.
- Generated fixtures are produced by a script in [`../tools`](../tools) and
  committed. Tests never need Python, CoolProp or network access to run.
- JSON is the default format, read with V's `json2` module.

| File | Contents | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| `m1_thermo.json` | PR and SRK, pure n-butane and a methane / n-butane / CO₂ ternary, computed by Caleb Bell's `thermo` (same equations and constants as reflux) | `thermo/fixtures_test.v`: agreement to 1e-9. `python/tests/test_thermo_reference.py`: the same through the C API and the Python package, with the fixture's constants given as the caller's own compounds: Z, V, ln φ, Hʳ and Sʳ to 1e-9 |
| `m1_coolprop_butane.json` | n-butane from CoolProp's reference equation, with PR's deviations from it at generation time | `thermo/fixtures_test.v`: PR's deviations match and haven't grown |
| `m2_tdep.json` | Every correlation form `tdep` supports, on real ChemSep 8.50 records and a few synthetic sets: value, dY/dT, ∫Y dT and ∫Y/T dT at 40 digits (mpmath), and `chemicals` 1.5.2 values for the DIPPR forms | `tdep/fixtures_test.v`: values to 1e-13, derivatives and integrals to 1e-11, `chemicals` to 1e-12 |
| `m2_coolprop.json` | The 85 CoolProp 8.0.0 fluids that ChemSep also has: CoolProp's Tc, Pc, ω, M, ideal-gas Cp and vapour pressure, with ChemSep's deviation from each at generation. Also n-butane's Psat at four temperatures and its enthalpy at ten states. | `components/coolprop_test.v`: each deviation, recomputed through reflux, matches and hasn't grown. `components/fluid_test.v`: the end-to-end Psat and enthalpy changes. |
| `m2_pr_psat.json` | Peng–Robinson's vapour pressure (Caleb Bell's `thermo` 0.6.1, from ChemSep's Tc, Pc, ω) against ChemSep's own correlation, for 20 representative compounds at Tr 0.5–0.95 | `components/quality/quality_test.v`: reflux's PR matches `thermo` to 1e-9, and each deviation matches and hasn't grown |
| `m3_pip.json` | Phase identification from Caleb Bell's `thermo` 0.6.1: 1,264 PR and SRK states (1,327 roots), pure components and mixtures across the saturation curve and the critical point, plus liquids squeezed to within 0.02% of the covolume, each root with its volume and analytic PIP. Also pure CO₂ through the Soave zero, T₀ = Tc(1 + 1/m)², with the properties M1 checks | `thermo/phase_test.v`: volumes to 1e-9, PIP to 1e-7, every label the same; CO₂ through T₀ to 1e-9 |
| `m3_stability.json` | 513 PR (and some SRK) states for stability: binaries on grids of T, P and z, 62 near the methane/n-butane critical locus (33 of them 0.1 bar apart), a ternary and a 10-component gas condensate. For each binary, a brute-force scan of the tangent-plane distance over the whole composition range; for every state, Caleb Bell's `thermo` 0.6.1 FlashVL (agreeing with the scans everywhere), with each split's phases as a witness of instability | `flash/stability_test.v`: every verdict, the scans' global minima to 1e-11, every instability proved and every incipient phase stationary, the trivial solution caught, split phases stable, and a recorded iteration budget |
| `m3_rachford_rice.json` | 87 seeded Rachford–Rice cases: 2 to 20 components, K from 1e-30 to 1e25, trace phases down to 1e-15, K within 1e-8 of 1, negative flashes and absent components. The reference is the exact root for each case's floats (bisection at 100 digits with mpmath 1.3.0), with what `chemicals` 1.5.2's own solvers return | `numeric/rachford_rice_test.v`: compositions to 1e-15, β and L to 4 ulps of what the K-values allow, and no larger an error than any of `chemicals`' float solvers |
| `m3_thermo.json` | The flash references, from Caleb Bell's `thermo` 0.6.1 with a shared quadratic ideal-gas Cp: 83 PT states (binaries, a ternary, the gas condensate, near-critical points, pure n-butane and CO₂, and narrow-boiling n-butane/isobutane), each with its split, fugacity residual and molar V, H, S and U, and where `thermo`'s own PH, PS and TV flashes land from them; 36 pure-component saturation states (`FlashPureVLS`); 42 bubble and dew points, polished by Newton on `thermo`'s own ln φ and each checked to be a phase boundary | `flash/thermo_test.v`: splits to 1e-8, V, H, S and U to 1e-9, saturation and boundary fugacities to 1e-10, Psat to 1e-9, and reflux's PT flash sees each boundary. `flash/vf_test.v`: the bubble and dew points and saturation states to 1e-11, and every PT split's vapour-fraction round trip to 1e-8. `flash/ph_test.v`: every PT state's PH and PS round trip, and every saturation state's, to 1e-8. `flash/tv_test.v`: the same for TV and UV. `python/tests/test_flash.py`: every PT state's split through the C API and the Python package, with the fixture's constants given as the caller's own compounds: splits to 1e-8 and the phases' V to 1e-9 (H and S aren't compared: the fixture's Cp isn't ChemSep's). `python/tests/test_flashes.py`: the bubble and dew points and saturation states through the package, to 1e-11 |
| `m3_bench.json` | `tools/gen_m3_bench.py`, by hand on Windows with DWSIM 9 | M3's benchmarks (D10, criterion 8): 12 cases (PT with two phases and one, PH by state, the bubble point at P, for 2, 5 and 10 components), 40 states each, with reflux's, thermo 0.6.1's and DWSIM 9's median and minimum times, timed case by case, and their answers at the first state. Peng–Robinson with DWSIM's constants and kᵢⱼ for all three programs. `benchmarks/benchmarks_test.v` checks that reflux's answers match; `tools/benchmarks.vsh` writes `docs/benchmarks.md` from it. The timings vary between runs, so this is the one fixture that can't be reproduced byte for byte. |
| `m4_bench.json` | `tools/gen_m4_bench.py`, by hand on Windows with DWSIM 9 | M4's flowsheet benchmark (D14, criterion 9): the reference flowsheet on DWSIM's constants, solved by DWSIM 9 (its default recycle tolerances, and them scaled by 1e-8) and by reflux (Wegstein and direct substitution), each time's first solves and solves again with the feed 0.01 K warmer, in milliseconds, with the passes and the products' flows. `benchmarks/flowsheet_test.v` checks that each program solved the same flowsheet and that the committed report shows every timing; `tools/benchmarks.vsh` writes it into `docs/benchmarks.md`. Its timings vary between runs, like `m3_bench.json`'s. |
| `m10a_bench.json` | `tools/gen_m10a_bench.py`, by hand with V and gcc | M10a's speed (criterion 10): properties and a PT flash of methane, ethane and n-butane at 20 bar, at 1, 100 and 10,000 points, each call's µs from V's own loop (`tools/bench_case.v --capi`) and from Python through the C API, alternately, with the machine, the build and NumPy's version. `benchmarks/flowsheet_test.v` checks that each is there and that the committed report shows it; `tools/benchmarks.vsh` writes it into `docs/benchmarks.md`. Its timings vary between runs, as `m3_bench.json`'s do. |
| `m3_dwsim.json` | 25 cases from DWSIM 9.0.5's Peng–Robinson package (PT, PH and PS by state, bubble and dew points) with DWSIM's constants, Cp and vapour-pressure coefficients, kᵢⱼ and flash settings. Each has DWSIM's answer and its own fugacity residual, the exact PR with the same constants (`thermo` 0.6.1, mpmath 1.3.0 for the Cp integrals), and the PR with DWSIM's rounded constants. Run by hand on Windows | `flash/dwsim_test.v`: reflux matches the exact PR to 1e-8 (split) and 1e-9 (H, S), is within 1e-4 of DWSIM and no further than the exact answer is, and DWSIM's differences are explained case by case. reflux's own bubble and dew points, and its PH and PS flashes by state, land on the exact PR's |
| `m4_units.json` | Every unit `quantity` accepts, from NIST SP 811 (2008), appendices B.8 and B.9: 67 factors to SI, each marked exact or as SP 811's 7 figures, and 13 affine conversions (Celsius, Fahrenheit, Rankine, gauge pressure). Written by hand | `quantity/quantity_test.v`: exact factors to 4 ulps, the rest round to SP 811's figures, the affine ones to 1e-12, and no accepted unit left out |
| `m9_units.json` | Every unit symbol `quantity` knows standing alone, one unit for each SI prefix, and compound units (kmol/(kg*h), J/(mol*K), bar^0.5, lb/ft^3, …): 101 factors to SI from NIST SP 811 (2008), appendices B.8 and B.9, each marked exact or as SP 811's 7 figures, with each unit's dimension as `quantity` writes it. Written by hand, the compound factors computed exactly with Python's `fractions` | `quantity/quantity_test.v`: exact factors to 4 ulps, the rest round to SP 811's figures, every dimension as written, and no symbol or prefix left out |
| `m9_expressions.json` | 260 expressions in reflux's syntax (52 by hand, for precedence, every function, every spelling of an operator and a rate's shape; 208 seeded), each read by SymPy 1.13.3 as Python syntax, its symbols positive, and valued by mpmath 1.3.0 at 50 digits at four points, with each point's scale (the largest magnitude of any subexpression) and its derivative with respect to each input; reflux's plain, Unicode and LaTeX renderings of each, which the generator decoded and found to mean the text at every point; and the built-in constants, from the SI Brochure's defining constants (R and F computed exactly), checked against SciPy 1.14.1's CODATA 2018. `tools/gen_m9_fixtures.py`, with V on the PATH | `expr/sympy_test.v`: each case to 1e-12 of its scale (8.3e-15 at worst), every rendering the confirmed one, every plain form reading back to the same tree, and each constant the double nearest its exact value. `expr/tape_test.v`: the tape's value eval's to the bit, and every derivative SymPy's to 1e-10 of the larger of the derivative, the scale and 1 (6.5e-16 at worst) |
| `m9_formulas.json` | Every component file's composition as two independent programs read it: RDKit 2024.9.6 from its SMILES string (each atom's element, hydrogens and formal charge, sanitized where RDKit allows), and chemicals 1.5.2 from its own database by CAS number (PubChem's formulas, for 639 of the 642), each in Hill's order; and chemicals' atomic weights for elements 1 to 92. `tools/gen_m9_reactions.py` | `components/formula_test.v`: reflux's SMILES reader gives RDKit's composition and charge for all 639 strings but ortho- and para-hydrogen's, which spell their names; every compound but the two mixtures has a formula two of its sources agree on, chemicals' for all 638 it has; the five files that disagree with themselves are the ones listed; and the standard atomic weights within 2e-4 of chemicals' (1.6e-4 at worst, sulfur's) |
| `m9_reactions.json` | Twelve reactions (reforming, the shift, methanol, ammonia, combustion, hydration, SO₂ oxidation, an isomerisation, two dehydrogenations) on ChemSep's data from the component files: ΔH°, ΔS°, ΔG°, ln K at 1 bar and d ln K/dT at 13 temperatures from 298.15 to 1500 K, each Cp correlation evaluated and integrated by mpmath 1.3.0 at 50 digits; Σν ΔG°f and its gap from ΔH°f and S°; ln K from thermo 0.6.1's own data; and equilibrium constants others fit, the owner's DWSIM case's (on pressures in atm) and those the literature uses with Xu and Froment's kinetics (in bar), with ln K's distance from reflux's. `tools/gen_m9_reactions.py` | `kinetics/standard_test.v`: every property to 1e-13 of its terms' magnitudes (1.3e-16 at worst), the gaps to 1e-9 J/mol, ln K's distance from thermo's data within each reaction's recorded bound, and the owner's correlations' distances as recorded |
| `m9_kinetics.json` | Xu and Froment's reforming kinetics (45 states, 700 to 1100 K, 1 to 30 bar) and Vanden Bussche and Froment's methanol kinetics (24 states, 473 to 563 K, 50 and 80 bar), each rate by mpmath 1.3.0 at 50 digits from the paper's own formulas, written independently of reflux, with its derivatives with respect to T and each partial pressure and its largest term. The constants are the papers' own: Xu and Froment's Tables 5 and 6, Vanden Bussche and Froment's Table 2 and Graaf's equilibrium constants as they print them, but Xu and Froment's K1 and K2, the correlations later papers use, their paper giving none. Each paper's centred table against its pre-exponential one, constant by constant, as a ratio beside its rounding (`agreement`): Xu and Froment's disagree by up to 1.72%. `tools/gen_m9_kinetics.py` | `kinetics/law_test.v`: the structured forms' rates to 1e-13 of their largest terms (9.4e-15 at worst), and their derivatives to 1e-12 (1.1e-14 at worst) |
| `m4_graphs.json` | 59 directed graphs with their nets, every elementary cycle, the exact minimum tears and the fewest second breaks. 9 are the classical test problems of Gundersen and Hertzberg (1983), read off the paper's figures and held by the generator to its tables (units, streams, nets, cycles and minimum tears); 10 are worked by hand; 40 are seeded, with self-loops and parallel streams | `flowsheet/graph_test.v`: nets, cycle counts, tears and second breaks exactly, every stream calculated before it's used, every tear needed, and the same plan whatever the order of the ports |
| `flowsheets/reference.toml` | M4's reference flowsheet as a file, written by hand | `flowsheet/file_test.v`: it builds, to the last bit, what the same flowsheet does in code, and it's the base of the wrong-field tests and the fuzzing. `flowsheet/report_test.v`: its report is its solution, number for number, and balances on its own numbers. `main_test.v` and `tools/check.vsh`: `reflux solve` on it. Step 8's golden flowsheets go here too |
| `m4_dwsim.json` | DWSIM 9.0.5's PR at flash tolerances 1e-8: 13 unit operations, each alone from a stated inlet, with every outlet and its duty or work; the reference flowsheet, its recycle's tolerances scaled by 1e-8 with no acceleration, and its balances; and the open loop, fed reflux's converged recycle. For each state, H by the exact PR with DWSIM's constants (thermo 0.6.1, mpmath 1.3.0 for the Cp) and by DWSIM's rounded PR, and the exact PR's own answers for the vapour-fraction heater, the pump and the expander. `tools/gen_m4_dwsim.py`, by hand on Windows | `flowsheet/dwsim_test.v`: every unit and stream within criterion 2's targets of DWSIM, or explained by reproducing DWSIM's number from its rounded constants, its pump's density or its mixing entropy, with bounds that can't grow |
| `m4_dwsim/components/` | DWSIM's Tc, Pc, ω, molar mass and ideal-gas Cp for the five compounds, as reflux component files with no formation data. Written by `tools/gen_m4_dwsim.py` | `flowsheet/dwsim_test.v`: the fluid built from them is DWSIM's |
| `flowsheets/reference_dwsim.toml` | The reference flowsheet on `m4_dwsim/components/` and DWSIM's kᵢⱼ. Written by `tools/gen_m4_dwsim.py` | `flowsheet/dwsim_test.v`; `reflux solve` runs it as it is |
| `flowsheets/no_recycle.toml`, `interlocking.toml`, `saturated_loop.toml` | Golden flowsheets (D13), written by hand: a chain on SRK with no loop, with a drum given a duty and a knockout drum that finds no liquid; the reference flowsheet's loop with a second recycle, two cycles torn together; and a loop of pure propane at saturation, torn on a two-phase stream | `flowsheet/golden_test.v`; `flowsheet/report_test.v` reports on `interlocking.toml` |
| `flowsheets/golden/*.json` | The golden flowsheets' reports, as `reflux solve --json` writes them: these three, the reference and `every_unit.toml`. `tools/golden.vsh`, run only when a change is meant to move the answers, or for a new version, which each carries. A changed one is named in the CHANGELOG's next entry, or `tools/release.vsh` holds the release | `flowsheet/golden_test.v`: each flowsheet solves again to 1e-9 of each value's scale, with the same passes |
| `flowsheets/every_unit.toml` | A flowsheet with a unit of each type, each specified a different way from the reference, on SRK with a kᵢⱼ set by hand. Written by hand (moved from `file_test.v` in M4 step 7) | `flowsheet/file_test.v`: it loads, solves to what its file says, writes back and loads again, and it's fuzzed. `flowsheet/report_test.v`: every unit type's report, and the JSON against docs/report-format.md |

The M1 files are written by
[`../tools/gen_m1_fixtures.py`](../tools/gen_m1_fixtures.py), the M2 files
by [`../tools/gen_m2_fixtures.py`](../tools/gen_m2_fixtures.py), and the M3
files by [`../tools/gen_m3_fixtures.py`](../tools/gen_m3_fixtures.py),
except `m3_dwsim.json` and `m3_bench.json`, which
[`../tools/gen_m3_dwsim.py`](../tools/gen_m3_dwsim.py) and
[`../tools/gen_m3_bench.py`](../tools/gen_m3_bench.py) write.
`m4_units.json` is written by hand from SP 811, which its header cites,
with SP 811's own entry beside each unit that it lists, and so is
`m9_units.json`. [`../tools/gen_m9_fixtures.py`](../tools/gen_m9_fixtures.py)
writes `m9_expressions.json`, running `../tools/expr_render.v` for reflux's
renderings, and [`../tools/gen_m9_reactions.py`](../tools/gen_m9_reactions.py)
writes `m9_formulas.json` and `m9_reactions.json`, and
[`../tools/gen_m9_kinetics.py`](../tools/gen_m9_kinetics.py) `m9_kinetics.json`.
[`../tools/gen_m4_graphs.py`](../tools/gen_m4_graphs.py) writes
`m4_graphs.json`, from networkx and scipy's exact integer programming.
[`../tools/gen_m4_dwsim.py`](../tools/gen_m4_dwsim.py) writes `m4_dwsim.json`,
`m4_dwsim/components/` and `flowsheets/reference_dwsim.toml`, and
[`../tools/golden.vsh`](../tools/golden.vsh) the golden reports in
`flowsheets/golden/`. [`../tools/gen_m4_bench.py`](../tools/gen_m4_bench.py)
writes `m4_bench.json`.
